Note model has title, body and timestamps

plan.summary: A REST API for managing personal notes. Clients (a web/mobile front end or scripts) call JSON endpoints to create, list, fetch, update and delete notes. Each note carries a title, body, and created/updated timestamps and is persisted in a single DynamoDB table. The service runs as a standalone FastAPI process that talks to DynamoDB directly via boto3; no asynchronous or event-driven processing is implied by the spec, so no queues, topics or Lambda functions are planned.

endpoints.purpose: Liveness/readiness probe used by the evaluation harness; reports service status and DynamoDB table reachability.
Create a new note from a JSON body containing title and body; generates a UUID id and created_at/updated_at timestamps, writes the item to DynamoDB, returns 201 with the created note.
List notes with optional pagination (limit and next_token cursor) via a DynamoDB scan; returns an array of notes plus a next token when more results exist.
Fetch a single note by id; returns 404 if the note does not exist.
Update the title and/or body of an existing note, refresh updated_at, and return the updated note; 404 if missing.
Delete a note by id; returns 204 on success and 404 if the note does not exist.

data_models.name: Note
fields: body: string (required, may be empty string)

data_models.name: NoteCreateRequest
fields: body: string (optional, defaults to empty string)

aws_resources.name: notes
aws_resources.justification: Primary persistence for note items as required by the spec ('Notes are stored in DynamoDB'). Single table with string partition key 'id', PAY_PER_REQUEST billing; read/written by every CRUD endpoint.

aws_resources.name: /cloudforge/personal-notes-api
aws_resources.justification: Log group the FastAPI service writes structured application and request logs to, giving observability for the CRUD operations. Only resource needed for operational visibility since the app is not Lambda-hosted.

aws_resources.name: notes-api-app-policy
aws_resources.justification: Least-privilege policy (and matching role/user for the service credentials) granting GetItem, PutItem, UpdateItem, DeleteItem, Query and Scan on the notes table plus CreateLogStream/PutLogEvents on the log group — exactly the API calls the application code makes.

assumptions: No authentication or multi-tenant user model was specified, so the API is single-user/unauthenticated and notes are not partitioned per user; the DynamoDB key is just the note id.
Note ids are server-generated UUID4 strings rather than client-supplied.
Timestamps (created_at, updated_at) are server-generated ISO-8601 UTC strings; created_at is immutable and updated_at is refreshed on every successful update.
Listing uses a DynamoDB Scan with a cursor-based next_token (default limit 50, max 100) because no sort order or index requirement was specified; no global secondary indexes are created.
PUT is treated as a partial update (fields omitted from the body are left unchanged) and returns 404 rather than upserting an unknown id.
Validation errors return 422, missing notes return 404, and all responses are JSON.
No file attachments, search, sharing, or background processing were requested, so S3, SQS, SNS, Lambda, API Gateway and Secrets Manager are intentionally omitted.
AWS endpoints, region and table name are supplied to the service through environment variables so it can point at LocalStack.
